chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
title: The trio's success and his short singing career with Route 66
summary: The trio works well around Washington, but his attempt to sing Nat Cole's Route 66 ends when he runs out of breath, and he never sings again.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Nevertheless, I had to finally tell Sarah that there just wasn't anything out here for a female singer. I never told her anything about these things. But I started to get work for the trio. And we worked quite a bit in the clubs around
here, and everybody liked the group.

I remember one time, the group was doing was so well... We used to play a lot of the things that Nat Cole's group was playing. So I decided that I was going to try to do some singing. So we had an arrangement on Nat Cole's "Route 66." The first night that we played this particular thing, we were working on a club up on Fourteenth Street -- I don't remember the name of it. But we started playing this number, and not having ever sung before in any kind of situation but perhaps school or church, I'm out here doing this thing and aping Nat Cole, and as many singers as I had worked with, I had never given any thought to proper breathing -- or breathing at all!

In this particular song, it has a passage in there, where he says, "You go through St. Louis and Joplin, Missouri, Oklahoma City looks mighty pretty, you see Amarillo, Gallup, New Mexico, Flagstaff, Arizona, don't forget Winona, Kingston, Bosco, San Bernardino..." And I sang that passage, and by the time I got to San Bernardino, I thought I was gonna die! I was gaspin' for breath. The audience was laughing, because they could hear me running out of breath. And what happened is that I didn't...I should have taken a breath before I started singing it.
Anyway, after that experience, that ended my career as a singer. And I haven't uttered a sound over a microphone since
in any nightclub! Because that convinced me that singing is for singers, and I should just stick to my piano where I felt comfortable and knew what I was doing. I hoped I did anyway.
But the trio lasted, I guess, about a year and a half, in which we played two or three clubs in Washington.
